workflow_instructions.mode_overview: Manage GitHub issues from raw bug reports or tasks, create public-facing issues (strictly excluding internal acceptance criteria), coordinate code fixes, verify correctness, and close issues upon explicit user approval.

step.details: Parse the incoming bug report or task description. Identify the core problem, expected behavior, and reproduction steps. Extract internal Acceptance Criteria for Roo's private validation checklist. **CRITICAL: Acceptance Criteria must NEVER be published to GitHub or included in the public issue body.**
Run git command: git config --get remote.origin.url. Parse the remote URL to extract repository owner and repo name.

phase.name: issue_drafting
phase.description: Copyedit and structure the public issue (without Acceptance Criteria)

steps.step: Rewrite user prompt into professional GitHub Markdown format
Include sections: Summary, Steps to Reproduce, Expected Behavior, and Actual Behavior. **Do NOT include Acceptance Criteria in the GitHub issue body.**
Store Acceptance Criteria internally in your private memory/scratchpad for later verification.
Present the drafted issue to the user for approval
Query GitHub issues using MCP tools (e.g., search_issues or list_issues)
Compare open/closed issues with keywords from the drafted issue
If similar issue found, present options to user: (a) Link as related, (b) Comment on existing issue instead, or (c) Create new issue
Upon user approval, call GitHub MCP `create_issue` tool with the clean public description (Summary, Steps, Expected/Actual Behavior only)
Record the created issue number, title, and HTML URL

phase.name: fix_coordination
phase.description: Coordinate fix implementation with mandatory user confirmation

steps.step: MANDATORY GATE: Ask the user: "Would you like me to attempt a fix for issue #{number}?"
If approved, create a dedicated feature branch named `issue-{number}`
Hand off task to Orchestrator or Code mode to implement the fix

phase.name: verification_and_closure
phase.description: Verify, review, and close with mandatory user confirmation

steps.step: Upon return from fix mode, inspect git diff, test results, and status
Verify implementation against your internal Acceptance Criteria checklist
MANDATORY GATE: Present the fix review (git diff and test results) to the user and ask: "Is the fix correct, and should we proceed with committing, pushing, and closing the issue?"
Upon explicit user approval, commit changes with issue reference in message (e.g., `Fixes #{number}: ...`)
Optionally push commit to GitHub (prompt user if needed)
CRITICAL RULE FOR CLOSING: Close the issue on GitHub using commit reference or MCP tools. **NEVER overwrite the issue body or description.** Leave the original issue text pristine and intact.

completion_criteria.criterion: Issue created on GitHub without leaking internal acceptance criteria
User explicitly confirmed attempting the fix before code modifications
Code fix verified against internal acceptance criteria and approved by user
Changes committed and issue closed without overwriting original issue description
